1832.narrator: Abū Tha'labah al-Khushanī Jurthūm ibn Nāshir (رضي الله عنه)
1832.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) made certain things obligatory, so do not neglect them. He laid down certain limits, so do not exceed them. He prohibited certain things, so do not indulge in them. He was silent about certain things as a mercy to you and not because of forgetfulness, so do not delve into them." (Dāraquṭnī, Ḥākim, Bayhaqī)
1832.commentary: Imām Sam'ānī (رحمه الله) stated that this ḥadīth occupies a pivotal role in Islām and that one who abides by its instructions will attain ultimate success. "Obligatory" things refer to matters which Islām regards as compulsory such as ṣalāh, fasting, zakāh, Ḥaj, etc. "Limits" refer to those matters which Islām has laid down penal punishments for such as adultery, theft, slander, etc.

1833.narrator: Abdullāh ibn Abī Aufā (رضي الله عنه)
1833.text: We went with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) on seven expeditions during which we ate locusts." Another narration has: "We ate locusts with him." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Nasa'ī)
1833.commentary: Consuming locusts is permissible according to all the four Imāms. It is not established that the Messenger (ﷺ) ever ate locusts, however he did not prevent the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) from doing so.

1834.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "A believer is not bitten from the same hole twice." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1834.commentary: During the era of the Messenger (ﷺ), there was a poet by the name of Abū Ghazzah. He would recite poetry inciting the enemies against Islām. He was captured during the battle of Badr and brought before the Messenger (ﷺ). He apologised for his wrongs and the Messenger (ﷺ) took an oath from him that he would not return to his old ways. However, he broke his oath and again began composing evil poetry. When he was captured during the battle of Uḥud, he again promised never to compose such poetry, but the Messenger (ﷺ) had him killed. When people questioned the Messenger (ﷺ) about this, he mentioned that a believer is not bitten from the same hole twice. The ḥadīth may also mean that a believer should be alert and vigilant regarding the plots of others; he should not allow himself to be continuously deceived.

1835.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh will not speak to three people on the day of Qiyāmah, nor will he look at them or purify them. For them will be a painful punishment. A person who has extra water in a desert land but refuses it to a traveller; a person who sells an item to another person after 'Aṣr and takes an oath in Allāh that he purchased it for such-and-such a price and the buyer believes him when it is not true; and a person who pledges allegiance to a leader solely for worldly gain. If the leader gives him, he remains loyal to him and if he does not give him, he opposes him." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Nasā'ī, Aḥmad)
1835.commentary: "Allāh will not speak to them," means: 1. Allāh (ﷻ) will ignore them. 2. Allāh (ﷻ) will not address them as He will address the righteous. 3. Allāh (ﷻ) will not speak to them in a manner that will benefit them. The time of 'Aṣr has been mentioned because it is a blessed time when the angels gather. Taking a false oath is ordinarily sinful, however to do so at this time and merely to make a sale is a grave sin. Pledging a deceptive oath to the khalīf of the Muslims is a grave sin because it leads to corruption and rebellion.

1836.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Between the two blowings of the Trumpet is forty." They asked: "Forty days?" He said: "I refuse to say." They asked: "Forty years?" He said: "I refuse to say." They asked: "Forty months?" He said: "I refuse to say." "Everything of a person will perish except the tailbone. From it the body will be created. Allāh will then send down rain from the sky and they will grow like plants." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1836.commentary: Shortly before Qiyāmah, Isrāfīl will blow the trumpet causing every person to become unconscious. He will then blow it a second time causing all of humanity to rise from their graves. This ḥadīth refers to the time interval between these two soundings of the trumpet. From other aḥādīth, we learn that the interval will be forty years. While every human body decomposes in its grave, the bodies of the Messengers of Allāh (ﷺ), the martyrs and the selected friends of Allāh (ﷻ) remain intact.

1837.text: While the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was in a gathering speaking to the people, a Bedouin came and asked: 'When is the Final Hour?' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) continued talking. Some in the gathering said, 'He heard what the man said but disliked it,' while others said, 'No, he did not hear it.' When the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) had finished speaking, he asked: 'Where is the person who asked about the Final Hour?' The man said: 'Here I am, O Messenger of Allāh!' The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'When trust is betrayed, await the Final Hour.' He asked: 'How will it be betrayed?' He replied: 'When positions of authority are assigned to those who are undeserving of it, await the Final Hour.'" (Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
1837.commentary: The ḥadīth means that when leadership is handed over to individuals who are undeserving of it such as women, brazen sinners, fraudsters, or unknowledgeable people, then Qiyāmah is close. Unsound leadership is detrimental because it allows the rights of people to be usurped. The ḥadīth may also mean that people who are ignorant will pass Islāmic verdicts, lead others in ṣalāh, etc.

1838.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "They (your leaders) will lead you in ṣalāh. If they lead you correctly, you will be rewarded. If they make a mistake, you will be rewarded and they will be responsible." (Bukhārī, Bayhaqī)
1838.commentary: The ḥadīth teaches us that people should not rebel against those who lead them in ṣalāh if the latter commit mistakes such as not fulfilling the Sunnah requirements, etc. People should continue following them in ṣalāh because ṣalāh is valid behind even a brazen sinner. However, if their mistakes entail actions which nullify ṣalāh such as omission of a Farḍ, then one is not obligated to follow them. Similarly, if they commit or enforce any such action which opposes the teachings of Islām, then they should not be obeyed, in accordance to the prophetic principle: "Creation cannot be obeyed by disobeying the Creator."

1839.text: Regarding the verse, "You are the best of nations appointed for people," "The people who are the most beneficial to others are those who bring others with chains around their necks until they embrace Islām." (Bukhārī)
1839.commentary: The verse means that the Ummah of Muḥammad (ﷺ) is superior to other Ummahs. The interpretation given here means that their superiority is on account of them bringing captives from their battles and then introducing them to Islām. This is a great virtue because, on the one hand, these brave individuals forsake their homes to spread the message of Allāh (ﷻ) to the world, and on the other hand, become a means of saving many from the punishment of the Hell-fire and entering them into Paradise.

1840.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) is most pleased with a people who enter Paradise in chains." (Bukhārī) This means that they are brought as prisoners, they then embrace Islām and gain entry into Paradise.

1841.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The most beloved of places in the sight of Allāh are the masjids and the most hated of places in the sight of Allāh are the market places." (Muslim, Bayhaqī)
1841.commentary: The masjids are most beloved to Allāh (ﷻ) because they are places of worship, obedience, tilāwah and dhikr. They are the fountainheads of knowledge and guidance. A ḥadīth states that the masjids stand out for the occupants of the heavens just as the stars stand out for the occupants of the earth. For these reasons and others, those who frequent the masjids are blessed with Allāh's (ﷻ) special mercy. The market places are most hated because they are places of deception, lies, fraud, cheating, greed, interest and broken promises. They lead people away from Allāh's (ﷻ) remembrance and attract them towards the futilities of this world. For these reasons, one should only go there to the extent of necessity.

1842.text: The Messenger (ﷺ) said: "If it is at all possible for you, do not be the first to enter the market place nor the last to leave it because it is the battle ground of Shaiṭān and the place where he hoists his flag." (Muslim) Al-Barqānī (رحمه الله) narrates it in his Ṣaḥīḥ from Salmān who narrated that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Do not be the first to enter the market place nor the last to leave it. It is where Shaiṭān lays his eggs and where they hatch." (Muslim)
1842.commentary: The ḥadīth means that Shaiṭān thrives in market places because of the many evils prevalent there. One should therefore minimise one's time there.

1843.text: 'Āṣim al-Aḥwal narrates from 'Abdullāh ibn Sarjis (رضي الله عنه) who said: "I said to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ): 'O Messenger of Allāh, may Allāh forgive you.' He replied: 'And you as well.' 'Āṣim said: I asked him: 'Did the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) seek forgiveness for you?' He replied: 'Yes, and for you as well.' He then recited this verse: 'Seek forgiveness for your sins and the sins of the believing men and women.'" (Muslim)
1843.commentary: Forgiveness in relation to the Messenger (ﷺ) refers to Allāh's (ﷻ) kindness upon him and his honourable status in Allāh's (ﷻ) sight because it is our belief that he was free from all sin. That the Messenger (ﷺ) reciprocated a kind gesture with similar kindness was an indication of his noble character.

1844.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Part of what people learnt from the words of the earlier Messengers is: 'If you have no shame, you may do whatever you like.'" (Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
1844.commentary: This ḥadīth does not give permission to commit evil, rather it is a warning and reprimand from Allāh (ﷻ) that the loss of shame is a stepping stone to immorality. The reason for this is that shame serves as a deterrent from sin because one who is aware that Allāh (ﷻ) or other people are watching, will be reluctant to perpetrate sin openly. The ḥadīth also informs us that modesty was a teaching of all the Messengers of Allāh (ﷺ), hence it should be among the inherent good qualities of every human being.

1845.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The first matter that will be decided between people on the day of Qiyāmah will be the shedding blood." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Nasā'ī)
1845.commentary: Among the rights of human beings, murder will be dealt with first on the day of Qiyāmah because it is a grave sin. Allāh (ﷻ) created life in man, and one who destroys such life destroys Allāh's (ﷻ) creation, hence He will severely punish those who commit murder. The Qur'ān mentions the seriousness of this crime in these words: Whoever purposely murders a believer, his punishment shall be Hell-fire where he shall live forever. Allāh shall be angry with him, curse him and prepare for him a dreadful punishment. (Sūrah al-Nisā', 93)

1846.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The angels were created from light, jinn were created from a flame of fire, and Ādam was created from what was described to you." (Muslim, Aḥmad, Bayhaqī)
1846.commentary: The ḥadīth indicates the power of Allāh (ﷻ) because He can create life in various forms through light, fire and sand. Man is created from a drop of sperm which is in turn formed by consuming food produced from the soil, hence it can be said that man is created from sand.

1847.text: The character of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was the Qur'ān." (Muslim, Aḥmad)
1847.commentary: The ḥadīth means that the Messenger (ﷺ) lived by the Qur'ān. He was pleased with what it declared Ḥalāl, he abstained from what it declared Ḥarām, he practised upon its etiquettes, and he did not exceed its restrictions. Scholars state that just as the meanings of the Qur'ān are unlimited, the qualities of the Messenger (ﷺ) portraying the excellence of his character were also unlimited. In every situation, his outstanding behaviour, sublime personality and supreme knowledge were matchless and indescribable. For these reasons, he served as a model and Messenger for not only human beings and jinn but the entire universe.

1848.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh desires to meet one who desires to meet Him, and Allāh dislikes to meet one who dislikes to meet Him." I asked: "O Messenger of Allāh, is it a dislike for death? All of us dislike death." He replied: "That is not what it means. Rather, when a believer is given the glad tidings of Allāh's mercy, His pleasure and His Paradise, he desires to meet Allāh, and Allāh also desires to meet him. When a disbeliever is given the tidings of the punishment and wrath of Allāh, he dislikes to meet Allāh, and Allāh also dislikes to meet him." (Muslim, Bukhārī, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah)

1849.narrator: Umm al-Mu'minīn Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy (رضي الله عنها)
1849.text: I went to visit the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) one night while he was in I'tikāf. I spoke to him and then stood up to leave. He stood up with me to accompany me. Two men from the Anṣār passed by. When they saw the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ), they hastened. He said to them: 'Take it easy. This is Ṣafiyyah bint Ḥuyayy.' They said: 'Glory be to Allāh, O Messenger of Allāh!' He said: 'Shaiṭān flows in the body of man like blood and I feared that he might implant evil thoughts – or things – into your hearts.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)
1849.commentary: Ibn Ḥajar (رحمه الله) stated the Messenger (ﷺ) clarified to the two Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهما) that the woman was his wife because even the slightest form of suspicion regarding his blessed being would have been detrimental to their īmān. "Shaiṭān flows in the body of man like blood," means that he moves in the body of man like blood flows in the blood vessels of the body. 'Allāmah Ṭībi (رحمه الله) stated that it means that just as blood flows easily throughout the body, Shaiṭān spares no effort in attempting to lead man astray. Based on this ḥadīth, scholars state that the righteous should go the extra mile to avoid places of suspicion and doubt.

1850.narrator: Abū al-Faḍl al-'Abbās ibn 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib (رضي الله عنه)
1850.text: I was present with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) during the expedition of Ḥunayn. Abū Sufyān ibn al-Ḥārith ibn 'Abd al-Muṭṭalib (رضي الله عنه) and I remained close to the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and did not leave him. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) was on a white mule. When the Muslims and polytheists faced each other in battle, the Muslims turned around and fled. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) began prompting his donkey towards the polytheists while I was holding its reins, stopping it from hastening forward. Abū Sufyān (رضي الله عنه) was holding the saddle of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: 'O 'Abbās, call those who pledged allegiance under the tree (at Bay'at al-Riḍwān).'" Al-'Abbās (رضي الله عنه), who had a loud voice, said: "I shouted in my loudest voice: 'Where are those who pledged allegiance under the tree?' By Allāh, they turned to my call just as a cow turns to the call of its calf. They said: 'Here we are, here we are.' And they fought against the disbelievers. The call to the Anṣār was made, saying: 'O people of Anṣār! O people of Anṣār!' The call was then confined to the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj. The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) remained on his mule and looked at them fighting as if he was stretching out his neck. He said: 'Now the oven is hot.' He then took some pebbles and threw them towards the disbelievers and said: 'They are defeated, by the oath of the Lord of Muḥammad.' I went to have a look and the battle was raging as it had been previously, but as soon as he threw those pebbles, I saw their strength waning and they fled." (Muslim, Ḥākim)
1850.commentary: Ḥunayn was a valley between Makkah and Ṭā'if where the tribe of Hawazin resided. They rose against the Muslims and fought them in battle in 8 Hijrī. Scholars state that the stones thrown by the Messenger (ﷺ) in that battle miraculously penetrated the eye of every disbeliever bringing victory to the Muslims. It was the assistance of Allāh (ﷻ) that came to the fore as the Qur'ān states: You did not throw when you threw, but it was Allāh Who threw. (Sūrah Anfāl, 17) A Muslim leader must be a model of bravery and courage.

1851.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "O people, Allāh is pure and accepts only that which is pure. Allāh issued the same command to the believers as He issued to the Messengers. He said: 'O Messengers, eat of the pure and do good,' and He said: 'O believers, eat of the pure which We provided you with.' He then mentioned a person who undertakes a long journey, with dishevelled hair and dusty clothing. He stretches out his hands towards the heavens saying: 'O my Sustainer! O my Sustainer!' But his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful, and his sustenance is unlawful. How can his supplication be accepted?'" (Muslim, Aḥmad)
1851.commentary: This ḥadīth highlights the fundamental Islāmic principle that a person should choose that which is Ḥalāl over that which is Ḥarām because the former draws him closer to Allāh (ﷻ) while the latter distances him from Allāh (ﷻ). The description provided in the ḥadīth convincingly highlights the importance of earning, consuming and utilising that which is Ḥalāl.

1852.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh will not speak to three people on the day of Qiyāmah, neither will He purify them nor look at them. For them will be a painful punishment: an old adulterer, a lying king, and a poor person who is proud." (Muslim, Aḥmad, Nasā'ī)
1852.commentary: This ḥadīth was mentioned in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 617. Qāḍi 'Iyāḍ (رحمه الله) stated that these three individuals have been specifically mentioned because their sin was unnecessary and could have been avoided quite easily: adultery is to be expected from a young man bursting with desires, not an old man; a king has power and authority and has no need to speak lies to prove his case; and pride is expected from the wealthy, not the poor.

1853.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Saiḥān, Jaiḥān, the Euphrates and the Nile are all rivers from Paradise." (Muslim, Aḥmad)
1853.commentary: This ḥadīth has been interpreted in various ways. Some scholars have stated that the source of these rivers may truly be in Paradise. Others state that their waters are sweeter than that of other rivers, hence they have been referred to as rivers of Paradise. Yet other scholars state that the cities through which they flow are blessed with īmān, hence their association with Paradise. The Oxus and Jaxartes are two major rivers of Central Asia. The Euphrates runs through Iraq, and the Nile through Egypt.

1854.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) held my hand and said: 'Allāh created the earth on Saturday; He created the mountains on Sunday; He created the trees on Monday; He created detestable things on Tuesday; He created light on Wednesday; He spread out the animals on earth on Thursday; and He created Ādam (عليه السلام) after 'Aṣr on Jumu'ah as His last creation in the last hour of the day, between 'Aṣr and the night.'" (Muslim, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1854.commentary: The ḥadīth informs us that Allāh's (ﷻ) final creation was Ādam (عليه السلام) who was created on Jumu'ah. From other aḥādīth we learn that the world will also terminate on the day of Jumu'ah.

1855.narrator: Abū Sulaymān Khālid ibn al-Walīd (رضي الله عنه)
1855.text: Nine swords broke in my hand in the battle of Mu'tah and only one small Yemeni sword remained with me." (Bukhārī)
1855.commentary: The Battle of Mu'tah took place in 8 Hijrī. The Messenger (ﷺ) had sent Ḥārith ibn Amīr (رضي الله عنه) with a letter inviting the Persian king to Islām, however enroute the Ṣaḥābī was killed by Sharaḥbīl. The Messenger (ﷺ) sent an army of 3000 Ṣaḥābah to avenge his murder. During the ensuing battle, Zaid ibn Ḥārithah (رضي الله عنه), Ja'far ibn Abī Ṭālib (رضي الله عنه) and 'Abdullāh ibn Rawāḥah (رضي الله عنه) each led the army, but were martyred in turn. Finally, Khālid ibn Walīd (رضي الله عنه) assumed leadership and the Muslims attained victory. This ḥadīth highlights his bravery and it was for this reason that the Messenger (ﷺ) gave him the title, 'the sword of Allāh.'

1856.text: He heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "When a judge passes judgment making every effort to be correct and then reaches the correct decision, he receives two rewards. When he passes judgment making every effort to be correct and reaches an incorrect decision, he receives one reward." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd)
1856.commentary: The ḥadīth teaches us that a competent and knowledgeable scholar or judge may engage in ijtihād. Ijtihād means to exercise judgment in order to determine the truth in legal matters regarding which no clear ruling exists in the Qur'ān and Sunnah. It further teaches us that such ijtihād will draw a reward whether the ultimate decision is correct or not.

1857.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Fever is from the intense heat of Hell, so cool it down with water." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Ḥākim)
1857.commentary: Scholars state that fever here does not include all types of fevers because in certain cases applying water to a fever will worsen it.

1858.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "If one who passes away has outstanding fasts, his next of kin should fast on his behalf." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Bayhaqī, Aḥmad)
1858.commentary: The preferred opinion based on this ḥadīth is that it is permissible to fast on behalf of a deceased person who has outstanding fasts. The 'next of kin' refers to a relative, whether he is an heir or not. According to the majority of scholars, namely Imām Abū Ḥanīfah (رحمه الله), Imām Shāfi'ī (رحمه الله) and Imām Mālik (رحمه الله), others may only give fidyā (compensation in kind) on behalf of the deceased who omitted fasts. According to Imām Aḥmad (رحمه الله), others may fast on behalf of the deceased to compensate for his missed fasts. Imām Aḥmad (رحمه الله) utilises this ḥadīth as his proof. The other scholars prove their case by stating that this ḥadīth is abrogated or that fidyā is the same as fasting.

1859.text: 'Auf ibn Mālik ibn al-Ṭufayl narrates that 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) was informed that 'Abdullāh ibn al-Zubayr (رضي الله عنه) said with regard to a certain transaction or gift which 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) had made: "By Allāh, if 'Ā'ishah does not abstain from this, I will impose restrictions on her." She said: "Did he really say that?" They replied: "Yes." She said: "I take an oath in the name of Allāh that I will never speak to Ibn al-Zubayr again." When the separation continued for some time, Ibn al-Zubayr (رضي الله عنه) asked someone to intercede on his behalf, but she said: "By Allāh, I will never accept intercession in this regard and I will never break my oath." When it had gone on too long for Ibn al-Zubayr (رضي الله عنه), he spoke to al-Miswar ibn Makhramah and 'Abd al-Raḥmān ibn al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yagūth, and said: "I beg you in the name of Allāh to take me to 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) because it is not lawful for her to take an oath to sever ties with me." So Al-Miswar and 'Abd al-Raḥmān went along with him and they two sought permission to enter the home of 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها). They said: "Peace be upon you together with Allāh's mercy and blessings. May we enter?" She said: "You may enter." They asked: "All of us?" She said: "Yes, you may all enter," not knowing that Ibn al-Zubayr (رضي الله عنه) was with them. When they entered, Ibn al-Zubayr (رضي الله عنه) went behind the curtain and embraced 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) weeping and beseeching her. Al-Miswar and 'Abd al-Raḥmān also began to beseech her to speak to him and accept his apology. They said: "You know very well that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) forbade the breaking of relations and said that it is not lawful for a Muslim to sever relations with his brother for more than three days." When they continued reminding and advising her, she began reminding them of her oath and began crying. She said: "I took an oath and an oath is a very serious matter." But they persisted until she spoke to Ibn al-Zubayr (رضي الله عنه). In expiation of her oath, she freed forty slaves. Whenever she subsequently remembered her oath, she would weep until her veil would become wet with her tears. (Bukhārī)
1859.commentary: 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) was the maternal aunt of 'Abdullāh ibn Zubayr (رضي الله عنه). He did not agree with a certain transaction she had made and tried to make her forsake it, however she felt offended because she had done it in good spirit. One may ask why 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) did not speak to her nephew for more than three days when the ḥadīth forbids it. The answer to this is that one may abandon ties with another based on a valid Islāmic reason. The freeing of a single slave would have sufficed, however 'Ā'ishah (رضي الله عنها) freed forty slaves due to her piety.

1860.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) went out to those who were martyred at Uḥud and supplicated for them (for forgiveness) eight years after the battle as if he was bidding farewell to the living and the dead. He then climbed onto the pulpit and said: 'I am your forerunner and I will be a witness for you. You will meet me at al-Ḥauḍ (the Fountain). I can see it from where I am now. Listen, I do not fear that you will ascribe partners with Allāh after me, but I do fear this world for you and that you will compete with each other for it.' That was the last time I saw the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) on the pulpit." Another narration has: "I am your forerunner and I will be a witness for you. By Allāh, I am presently looking at my Ḥauḍ. I have been given the keys to the treasures of the earth – or the keys to the earth. By Allāh, I do not fear that you will ascribe partners with Allāh after me, but I do fear that you will compete with each other for it." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Bayhaqī, Nasā'ī)
1860.commentary: The ḥadīth teaches us to be wary of competing for this world and its riches. The Messenger (ﷺ) was given the keys to the treasures of this world but he refused it due to his preference for the Hereafter. One should visit the graveyard and also continuously supplicate for the forgiveness of the deceased. The Ḥauḍ is a reality and exists just as Paradise and Hell exists.

1861.narrator: Abū Zayd 'Amr ibn Akhṭab al-Anṣārī (رضي الله عنه)
1861.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) led us in the Fajr ṣalāh and then climbed the pulpit and addressed us until the Ẓuhr ṣalāh. He descended, performed ṣalāh, and climbed the pulpit again until the 'Aṣr ṣalāh. He descended the pulpit, performed ṣalāh, and climbed the pulpit again until sunset. He informed us of what had occurred and what is yet to occur. The most knowledgeable of us is the one who remembers the most." (Muslim)
1861.commentary: The Messenger (ﷺ) informed the Ṣaḥābah (رضي الله عنهم) about the events that will unfold close to Qiyāmah. This knowledge was granted to him by Allāh (ﷻ) as a miracle. It was not on account of his own knowledge. It was the mercy of the Messenger (ﷺ) that he taught the Ummah whatever was necessary for their eternal success and well-being in this world.

1862.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "One who takes a vow to obey Allāh should obey Him. One who takes an oath to disobey Allāh should not disobey him." (Bukhārī, Aḥmad, Abū Dāwūd, Ibn Mājah)
1862.commentary: Oaths that conform to Islāmic teachings should be fulfilled, while those that oppose them should be broken.

1863.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) ordered her to kill chameleons, saying: "It blew on Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) (in the fire)." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1863.commentary: That a chameleon blew into the fire in which Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) was thrown, in order to intensify it, was evidence of its enmity to a Messenger of Allāh (عليه السلام). The ḥadīth teaches us that Allāh (ﷻ) dislikes even the slightest dissent or disobedience to His commands.

1864.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "One who kills a chameleon with the first strike, will receive such-and-such good deeds. One who kills it with the second strike, will receive such-and-such good deeds, less than the first. If he kills it with the third strike, he will receive such-and-such good deeds." Another narration has: "One who kills a chameleon with the first strike, a hundred good deeds are recorded in his favour. The second strike has less than that, and the third strike has even less than that." (Muslim)

1865.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "A man said: 'I will definitely give some charity.' He went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a thief. The next morning, people began talking: 'Charity was given to a thief.' The man said: 'O Allāh, all praise is due to You for a thief. I will definitely give some charity.' He went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a prostitute. The next morning, people began talking: 'Charity was given to a prostitute last night.' The man said: 'O Allāh, all praise is due to You for a prostitute. I will definitely give some charity.' He went out with his charity and placed it in the hand of a rich person. The next morning, people began talking: 'Charity was given to a rich person.' The man said: 'O Allāh, all praise is due to You for a thief, a prostitute and a rich person.' That night he saw a dream in which he was told: 'Perhaps your charity to the thief will cause him to abstain from stealing. Perhaps your charity to the prostitute will cause her to abstain from prostitution. Perhaps your charity to the rich person, will cause him to take a lesson and spend from that which Allāh gave him.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1865.commentary: The ḥadīth teaches us that Allāh (ﷻ) rewards a person based on his intention and not merely on the outcome of his action. Hence, if charity is given with sincerity and reaches one who is not really deserving of it, the donor should regard it as Allāh's (ﷻ) wisdom and remain hopeful of divine reward. It also teaches us that we should continue giving charity for the pleasure of Allāh (ﷻ).

1866.text: We were with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) at a feast. The foreleg of the meat was presented to him which was his favourite part. He took a bite from it and said: 'I am the leader of mankind on the day of Qiyāmah. Do you know why? Allāh will gather the first and the last on one plain where an observer will be able to see all of them and a caller will be able to make all hear him. The sun will draw close to them and people will experience such grief and distress that they will not be able to bear. The people will say: "Don't you see what has befallen you?" Some will say to others: "Go to your father Ādam." They will come to Ādam and say: "O Ādam, you are the father of mankind. Allāh created you with His hand, blew into you from His spirit, commanded the angels to prostrate before you and allowed you to dwell in Paradise. Will you not intercede for us before your Lord? Don't you see what we are experiencing?" He will reply: "My Lord is angry today with an anger like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after. He forbade me from the tree but I disobeyed. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone else, go to Nūḥ." They will come to Nūḥ and say: "O Nūḥ, you are the first Messenger to the people of the earth and Allāh has named you a grateful servant. Will you not intercede for us before your Lord?" He will reply: "My Lord is angry today with an anger like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after. I made a supplication against my people. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone else, go to Ibrāhīm." They will come to Ibrāhīm and say: "O Ibrāhīm, you are the Prophet of Allāh and His friend from among the people of the earth. Intercede for us before your Lord." He will say: "My Lord is angry today with an anger like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after. I had told three lies. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone else, go to Mūsā." They will come to Mūsā and say: "O Mūsā, you are the Messenger of Allāh. Allāh favoured you with His message and conversation above all people. Intercede for us before your Lord." He will say: "My Lord is angry today with an anger like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after. I had killed a person whom I was not commanded to kill. Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone else, go to 'Īsā." They will come to 'Īsā and say: "O 'Īsā, you are the Messenger of Allāh and His word which He cast to Maryam, and a spirit from Him. You spoke to people in the cradle. Intercede for us before your Lord." 'Īsā will say: "My Lord is angry today with an anger like of which He has never been angry before and will never be angry after." He did not mention any sin. "Myself, myself, myself. Go to someone else, go to Muḥammad."' In another narration: 'They will come and say: "O Muḥammad, you are the Messenger of Allāh and the seal of the Prophets. Allāh has forgiven your past and future sins. Intercede for us before your Lord. Don't you see what we are experiencing?" I will proceed until I reach below the Throne and fall prostrate before my Lord. Then Allāh will open to me such praises and glorification which He did not open to anyone before me. It will then be said: "O Muḥammad, raise your head. Ask and you will be given, intercede and your intercession will be accepted." I will raise my head...'" (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1866.commentary: This ḥadīth describes the agonising scenario on the day of Qiyāmah when all of humanity will anxiously await the commencement of the reckoning. They will approach various Messengers (عليهم السلام) but each of them will excuse himself. They will finally approach the only person worthy of this honour, the Messenger (ﷺ). Allāh (ﷻ) has kept this sequence in order to reveal the Messenger's (ﷺ) superiority over all the Messengers (عليهم السلام). He will then praise Allāh (ﷻ) in words beyond description and Allāh (ﷻ) will allow him to intercede for his Ummah. This is his lofty and prestigious position referred to in the Qur'ān: Soon Your Lord will accord to you the Maqām Maḥmūd. (Sūrah al-Isrā', 79)

1867.text: Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) brought the mother of Ismā'īl and her son, Ismā'īl, whom she was suckling, and left her by the House near a large tree above Zamzam at the highest point of the masjid. At the time, no one resided in Makkah and there was no water. He left them there with a bag of dates and a water-skin. Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) then turned and began to leave on the path he had come. The mother of Ismā'īl (عليه السلام) followed him and asked: 'O Ibrāhīm! Where are you going, leaving us in a valley where there is no companionship or anything else?' She repeated the question several times but he paid no attention to her. She asked: 'Has Allāh ordered you to do this?' He replied: 'Yes.' She said: 'In that case, He will not allow harm to come to us,' and went back. Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) continued until he reached al-Thanīyyah, where they could not see him. He turned towards the House and supplicated, raising his hands: 'O our Sustainer! I have settled some of my offspring in a valley that is barren, near Your Sacred House. O our Sustainer! So that they may establish ṣalāh. Therefore, make the hearts of some people to incline towards them and provide them with fruits, perhaps they may be grateful.' (Sūrah Ibrāhīm, 37)" He then narrated the ḥadīth in full. (Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
1867.commentary: Hājirā was a Coptic woman who was given to Sārah, the wife of Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام), as a gift by the king of Egypt. Ibrāhīm (عليه السلام) then married Hājirā. Hājirā's contentment with Allāh's (ﷻ) order to her husband was astonishing. The firmness of her īmān led her to easily accept that by accepting Allāh's (ﷻ) command, He would never allow harm to come to her or her son. Her sacrifice and effort was so beloved to Allāh (ﷻ) that He enshrined her search for water as an incumbent ritual of Ḥaj and 'Umrah.

1868.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "The mushroom is a type of manna and its water is a cure for the eyes." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1868.commentary: Manna was a type of food which Allāh (ﷻ) provided as sustenance to the Banū Isrā'īl. According to the scholars, mushrooms have been compared to manna because both these foods are acquired without effort or cultivation.

1869.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Cloudiness comes over my heart and I seek forgiveness from Allāh a hundred times a day." (Muslim, Aḥmad)
1869.commentary: The "cloudiness" referred to here is not a solid barrier. It is merely a partial covering similar to a light cloud in the sky which does not block out the rays of the sun. Scholars have provided various explanations: 1. The Messenger (ﷺ) would occasionally be occupied in something which prevented him from his routine state of remembering Allāh (ﷻ) such as eating, engagement with family, etc. This was by no means a shortcoming, however he considered it to be a shortcoming because of his piety. 2. The Messenger (ﷺ) would sometimes choose rukhṣah (concessionary law) instead of 'azīmah (absolute law) or he would choose the less preferable of two permissible options. When he would later come to realise that he could have chosen better, he would be greatly distressed.

1870.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "By Allāh, I seek forgiveness from Allāh and turn to Him in repentance more than seventy times a day." (Bukhārī)

1871.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "By the oath of that Being in whose control is my life, if you do not commit sins, Allāh will remove you and replace you with a people who will commit sins and seek forgiveness from Allāh, and He will forgive them." (Muslim)
1871.commentary: The ḥadīth does not mean that sin is encouraged, rather it highlights Allāh's (ﷻ) mercy and forgiveness and that, at times, sin is a means towards safety from pride. In other words, it encourages us to engage in abundant repentance for the sins we are bound to commit as Allāh (ﷻ) never fails to accept those who turn to Him. Allāh (ﷻ) loves a repentant sinner more than one who is content with his good actions because the former turns to Allāh (ﷻ) and expresses his weakness while the latter exhibits pride.

1872.text: We used to sit in the gathering of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) and count him saying a hundred times: 'O my Sustainer! Forgive me and turn to me. You are Forgiving, Merciful.'" (Abū Dāwūd, Tirmidhī)
1872.commentary: Aḥādīth which mention the abundant repentance of the Messenger (ﷺ) do not imply that he committed sin, but serve as encouragement for his Ummah to do likewise. It is also possible that because of his continuous advancement in spirituality, he regarded his past state as one worthy of repentance.

1873.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When a person regularly seeks forgiveness, Allāh provides for him a way out of every difficulty, relieves him from every anxiety, and provides him with sustenance from avenues he never expected." (Abū Dāwūd)

1874.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "One who says, 'I seek forgiveness from Allāh apart from whom there is none worthy of worship, the Living, the All-Sustaining, and I turn to Him in repentance,' will have his sins forgiven even if he fled from the battlefield." (Abū Dāwūd, Ḥākim)
1874.commentary: According to Abū Nu'aym al-Iṣbahānī (رحمه الله), this ḥadīth proves that some major sins are forgiven by virtue of repentance. These major sins exclude sins related to the rights of human beings.

1875.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The best way of seeking forgiveness is for a servant to say: 'O Allāh! You are my Sustainer. There is none worthy of worship besides You. You created me and I am Your servant. I will abide by Your covenant and Your promise to the best of my ability. I seek refuge in You from the evil which I have committed. I acknowledge Your bounties on me, and I acknowledge my sins, so forgive me. None forgives sins except You.' One who says these words during the day with total conviction in them and passes away before the evening, will be from the people of Paradise. One who says them at night and passes away before the next morning, will be from the people of Paradise." (Bukhārī, Aḥmad)
1875.commentary: This du'ā' is said to be the best way of seeking forgiveness because, according to Ibn Abī Jamrah (رحمه الله), it incorporates various profound meanings and beautiful words of expression. In it a person acknowledges Allāh's (ﷻ) Oneness and that He is the Creator, and he admits to the covenant made to Allāh and expresses hope of Allāh's (ﷻ) promises. One acknowledges his evil and the bounties of His Sustainer, and attributes sin to himself. He displays his desire for attaining forgiveness and confesses that none but Allāh (ﷻ) can forgive him.

1876.text: When the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) used to complete his ṣalāh, he would seek forgiveness three times and say: 'O Allāh, You are peace and all peace is from You. You are most blessed, O possessor of might and honour!'" Al-Auzā'ī, one of the narrators of this ḥadīth, was asked: "How should one seek forgiveness?" He replied: "Say, 'I seek forgiveness from Allāh. I seek forgiveness from Allāh.'" (Muslim, Aḥmad, Nasā'ī)
1876.commentary: This ḥadīth was mentioned in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 1415.

1877.text: Before the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) passed away he used to excessively say: 'Glory be to Allāh and praise be to Him. I seek forgiveness from Allāh and I turn to Him in repentance.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Nasā'ī)
1877.commentary: This ḥadīth was mentioned in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 114. It teaches that one should increase in good deeds towards the end of one's life in emulation of the practice of the Messenger (ﷺ). It also teaches us that īmān in Allāh (ﷻ) is a prerequisite for forgiveness because it is the foundation for the acceptance of good deeds. Without īmān, one cannot be forgiven, nor will one receive any reward in the Hereafter for any of his good deeds.

1878.text: I heard the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) saying: "Allāh (ﷻ) says: 'O son of Ādam! I will forgive you as long as you continue supplicating to Me and having hope in Me and I will not mind. O son of Ādam! I will forgive you even if your sins reach the height of the skies and you then seek forgiveness from Me and I will not mind. O son of Ādam! If you come to Me with sins equivalent to the size of the earth and you then meet Me without having ascribed any partners with Me, I will come to you with the equivalent amount of forgiveness.'" (Tirmidhī)
1878.commentary: This ḥadīth was mentioned in a previous chapter. See ḥadīth 442. It is repeated here to emphasise the overwhelming mercy of Allāh (ﷻ) and that one should never regard one's sins as too great for Allāh (ﷻ) to forgive.

1879.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of women! Give ṣadaqah and seek forgiveness in abundance because I have seen that you are the majority of the inmates of the Hell-fire." One of the women asked: "Why are we the majority of the inmates of the Hell-fire?" He replied: "You curse a lot and you are ungrateful to your husbands. Despite the fact that I see you deficient in intellect and religion, you can overpower a man of intelligence." She asked: "What is the deficiency in our intellect and religion?" He said: "The testimony of two women is equal to that of one man, and there are some days when you do not perform ṣalāh (due to menstruation)." (Muslim, Aḥmad, Ibn Mājah)
1879.commentary: "You are ungrateful to your husbands," means that women generally deny the favours and goodness of their husbands. A narration of Bukhārī explains this further: "If you are good to her for a long period of time and she happens to notice an error from you, she will say that she never saw any goodness in you." "You can overpower a man of intelligence," means that men are frequently overwhelmed by women due to the latter's temptations and plots.

1880.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The inhabitants of Paradise will eat and drink. They will have no need to defecate, blow their noses or urinate, rather, their food will produce a burp with the fragrance of musk. Glorifying Allāh (tasbīḥ) and expressing His greatness (taḥmīd) will be as natural to them as breathing." (Muslim)
1880.commentary: Paradise is a place of pristine purity. It is free of all forms of impurity, filth or dirt. A Muslim scholar was once asked how it was possible for Muslims to believe that they would not defecate or urinate in Paradise despite eating food. He replied that the concept was not farfetched because a foetus in the mother's womb is nourished with food but does not defecate or urinate. Imām Qurṭubī (رحمه الله) stated that the dhikr of the people of Paradise has been compared to breathing because both are performed without any effort. They will instinctively praise and glorify Allāh (ﷻ) because their hearts will be radiant and overflowing with Allāh's (ﷻ) recognition and love.

1881.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) said: 'I have prepared for My righteous servants that which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has imagined.' Read if you wish: 'No soul knows what pleasures are hidden for him as a reward for the deeds he carries out.'" (Sūrah al-Sajdah, 17) (Bukhārī, Muslim)

1882.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The first group to enter Paradise will be like the full moon. The next group will be like the brightest star in the sky. They will have no need to urinate, defecate, spit or blow their noses. Their combs will be of gold and their perspiration of musk. Their burners will burn fragrant aloes-wood. Their wives will be the wide-eyed damsels. All the men will be in appearance like their father, Ādam, sixty cubits in length." Another narration has: "Their utensils will be of gold and their perspiration of musk. Each of them will have two wives whose shin bones will be seen through the flesh because of their beauty. There will be no differences between them nor any hatred. Their hearts will be united, glorifying Allāh morning and evening." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad)
1882.commentary: Some may ask why they will have fragrant burners when their bodily fragrance will be one of musk. The answer is that the fragrances of Paradise will be merely for pleasure and enjoyment and not due to necessity. Men in Paradise will all be handsome in form and features. None will be excessively tall, short, fat or thin. They will be around 30 meters in length because Paradise will similarly be huge in size. Each man will have a minimum of two wives excluding the damsels. The reference to their shin bones being seen through the flesh is to indicate their exceptional purity and beauty. Their hearts will be united and free from hatred because they will be purified of every distasteful quality before entering Paradise.

1883.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Mūsā (عليه السلام) asked his Sustainer: 'Who will have the lowest rank in Paradise?' He replied: 'It will be a person who will come after all the inhabitants of Paradise have entered Paradise and he will be told: "Enter Paradise." He will ask: "O my Sustainer! How can I when the people have already settled down in their places and taken what has been prepared for them?" He will be told: "Would you be pleased if you have a kingdom like that of one of the kings of the world?" He will reply: "I will be pleased, O my Sustainer!" Allāh will say to him: "You have that, and the like thereof, and the like thereof, and the like thereof, and the like thereof." When it is said to him the fifth time, he will say: "I am pleased." Allāh will say: "You will have that and ten times the like thereof. You will have whatever your heart desires and whatever pleases your eye." He will say: "I am pleased, O my Sustainer!" (Mūsā عليه السلام) asked: "O my Sustainer! Who will be the highest in rank?" Allāh replied: "For those whom I choose, I have prepared their honour with My hands and I have sealed it. It is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart has imagined."' (Muslim)
1883.commentary: That the one lowest in rank will enjoy such a Paradise, speaks volumes of Allāh's (ﷻ) kindness and grace upon His servants.

1884.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "I know who will be the last to leave the Hell-fire and the last to enter Paradise. He will come out from the Hell-fire dragging himself on the ground. Allāh (ﷻ) will say to him: 'Go and enter Paradise.' He will go to Paradise and it will appear full to him. He will therefore turn back and say: 'O my Sustainer! I found it full.' Allāh (ﷻ) will say: 'Go and enter Paradise.' He will go to Paradise and it will appear full to him. He will therefore turn back and say: 'O my Sustainer! I found it full.' Allāh (ﷻ) will say: 'Go and enter Paradise. You will have a place the size of this world and ten times more – or you will have a place ten times this world.' He will say: 'Are You making fun of me – or are You joking with me – when You are the King?'" Ibn Mas'ūd (رضي الله عنه) said: "I saw the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) laughing until his molars were visible. He was saying: 'That will be the lowest of people in rank in Paradise.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim, Ibn Mājah)
1884.commentary: The Messenger (ﷺ) laughed because of the manner in which the servant of Allāh (ﷻ) will question his Sustainer.

1885.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "In Paradise, the believer will have a tent made of a single hollow pearl. It will be sixty miles high. The believer shall have family there and he will go around visiting them, but they will not see each other." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1885.commentary: The huge size of the homes of Paradise are an indication of its vastness. That a believer will have family (wives) and each will not see the other, further indicates to the vastness of the homes in Paradise.

1886.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "In Paradise there is a tree beneath which a strong, healthy, swift rider will not be able to ride across in a hundred years." Another narration from Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) has: "A rider will not be able to cross its shade in a hundred years." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1886.commentary: The extended shade of the trees of Paradise should serve to encourage people to live such lives in this world which will make them eligible to be from its inhabitants.

1887.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise will look up at the people in apartments above them just as you look at a glittering star moving on the horizon from the east or the west because of the difference in rank between them." The Ṣaḥābah said: "O Messenger of Allāh! Will those be the ranks of the Messengers which only they will attain?" He said: "No, by the oath of that Being in whose control is my life, they are people who believed in Allāh and accepted the Messengers." (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1887.commentary: This ḥadīth explains that the distance between any particular group in Paradise and those above them will be like the distance between the earth and the sky.

1888.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The length of a bow in Paradise is better than everything upon which the sun rises or sets." (Bukhārī)
1888.commentary: The smallest space or object in Paradise is far superior to the entire world because the former is eternal and everlasting while the latter is transient.

1889.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "There is a market-place in Paradise to which the people will go every Jumu'ah. The northerly wind will blow, brushing over their faces and clothes causing their beauty and handsomeness to increase. They will return to their families with increased beauty and handsomeness. Their families will say to them: 'By Allāh, you have become more beautiful and handsome.' They will reply: 'By Allāh, you have also become more beautiful and handsome since we left.'" (Muslim)
1889.commentary: This ḥadīth describes the fragrant breeze that will aromatise the inhabitants of Paradise. It also indicates to the mutual love and joy that will exist between families in Paradise. The northerly wind has been mentioned because it generally brings rain to the Arab lands. Scholars state that just as the women of Paradise will not go to the market places of Paradise, they should also not go to the shopping malls, bazaars and markets in this world, except due to necessity.

1890.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "The people of Paradise will look at the upper apartments of Paradise just as you look at the stars in the sky." (Bukhārī, Muslim, Tirmidhī)

1891.text: I was present in a gathering of the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) in which he described Paradise. Towards the end of his discussion, he said: 'In it is what no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no heart of man has imagined.' He then recited: 'Their sides remain away from their sleeping places, calling on their Sustainer with fear and longing. And they spend out of what We provided for them. No soul knows what pleasures are hidden for him as a reward for the deed he carried out.'" (Sūrah al-Sajdah, 16-17) (Bukhārī, Muslim)
1891.commentary: This ḥadīth explains that one of the many rewards of performing Tahajjud Ṣalāh is that one will be greatly rewarded in Paradise. Scholars state that this ḥadīth proves that aḥādīth are a commentary of the Qur'ān. In other words, the Qur'ān can only be correctly understood by a sound understanding of the aḥādīth.

1892.narrator: Abu Sa'id al-Khudri and Abu Hurayrah (ra)
1892.text: Abū Sa'īd al-Khudrī (رضي الله عنه) and Abū Hurayrah (رضي الله عنه) narrate that the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, an announcer will proclaim: 'You will live and never die. You will be healthy and never fall ill. You will be young and never grow old. You will have bounties and never experience misery.'" (Muslim)
1892.commentary: Unlike this worldly life, the bounties and pleasures of Paradise will be perpetual and everlasting. There will be no suffering or hardship of any sort, in accordance with the Qur'ānic verse: No difficulty shall afflict them there, neither will they be removed from there. (Sūrah al-Ḥijr, 48)

1893.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) will say to the one with the lowest rank in Paradise: 'Make a wish.' He will wish and wish. He will then ask him: 'Have you wished?' He will reply: 'Yes.' He will say to him: 'You have whatever you wished for and the like thereof.'" (Muslim)

1894.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "Allāh (ﷻ) will say to the inhabitants of Paradise: 'O inhabitants of Paradise!' They will reply: 'We are at your service, O our Sustainer, and we are pleased to be here. All good is in Your control.' Allāh will ask: 'Are you pleased?' They will reply: 'O our Sustainer! Why should we not be pleased when You have given us what You have not given any of Your creation?!' Allāh will ask: 'Should I not give you something better than that?' They will ask: 'What could be better than that?' Allāh will say: 'I bestow My pleasure upon you after which I will never be angry with you.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim, Tirmidhī)

1895.text: We were once with the Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) as he looked at the full moon. He said: 'You will see your Sustainer in person just as you are seeing this moon. Your view of Him will not be impeded.'" (Bukhārī, Muslim, Aḥmad, Tirmidhī)
1895.commentary: The sight of Allāh (ﷻ) has been compared to the full moon because of the absolute certainty of the sighting as well as the ease with which it will happen.

1896.text: The Messenger of Allāh (ﷺ) said: "When the people of Paradise enter Paradise, Allāh will ask them: 'Do you desire that I give you anything more?' They will reply: 'Have You not illuminated our faces? Have You not admitted us into Paradise and saved us from the Hell-fire?' The veil will then be lifted and they will not have been given anything that was more beloved to them than seeing their Sustainer." (Muslim, Ḥākim)
1896.commentary: This ḥadīth is supported by the Qur'ānic verse: Many faces on that day will be resplendent looking at their Sustainer. (Sūrah Qiyāmah, 22-23) O Allāh, grant us the good fortune of viewing Your blessed countenance, O Most Merciful of those who show mercy!
